integration_issues.issue: The useSiteConfig hook caches the merged config at module scope (`let cached = null`). After an admin saves (/api/admin/site-config) and the user navigates in SPA to '/', the cached value is reused and the UI only shows the new value after a hard reload. Our Playwright run saw hero title update because the hard-reload path happened; the announcement enable→disable→enable sequence appeared to NOT re-render until a cross-tab hard reload. Low priority but worth invalidating `cached` on 401 and on an explicit refresh() call wired into SiteConfigAdmin save success.

action_items: (low) Invalidate siteConfig.js module cache on PUT success in SiteConfigAdmin.jsx (expose a refresh() from useSiteConfig/loadSiteConfig and call it after save+reset) so SPA-navigated pages pick up the new config without a hard reload. The test harness worked around this by using a second tab + full reload.

(nit) /api/site-config PUT currently silently drops unknown top-level keys (good) but accepts any shape under a known key (e.g. {hero:{foo:'bar'}}) — consider validating against a Pydantic model per section for defence in depth.
critical_code_review_comments: cms_api.py `_process` recurses dicts/lists and traditionalises any Chinese string whose key is not in TEXT_SKIP_KEYS. TEXT_SKIP_KEYS currently is ('link','image','mobile_image','action','cover','id'). If a future section adds a URL-like field named e.g. 'href' or 'url', the string is still subject to traditional conversion — add 'url','href','slug','target' to the skip list proactively.

cms_api.article_visible_query uses an ISO-8601 string compare for start_at/end_at. This only works because inputs are also normalised to ISO strings with offset. Any client that passes a naive 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (as `published_at` uses) would sort incorrectly. Store dates as `datetime` in Mongo (BSON Date) and compare against `datetime.utcnow()`; current string compare is brittle to timezone & format mix.

cms_api._prep hard-codes `max_mb=4` for data-URL uploads of cover; the same limit is used for logo/banner uploads in `_process`. For hero / detail-banners (full-bleed PC images) 4MB can be tight — expose via env.

ActivitiesAdmin.jsx uses window.confirm for delete and native datetime-local for start_at/end_at. The datetime-local input renders the browser's default picker instead of a shadcn calendar, inconsistent with the rest of the admin UI (see system-prompt design hint about avoiding default browser pickers).

siteConfig.js `let cached = null` module-level cache has no public invalidate method; SiteConfigAdmin.jsx save/reset handlers can't nudge it, so other mounted pages keep the stale value until a hard reload (see integration_issues).

cms_api.py has NO auth check on `/api/articles/{id}` versus `article_visible_query` — the public detail endpoint (in server.py L361-380) must also enforce the visibility rules; otherwise an expired/scheduled/inactive article could still be read if its ID is known. Please confirm the server.py handler ANDs the visibility query (not tested here; only list behaviour was tested).

rca of the issue: No real bugs this iteration. The one soft-finding is a SPA cache issue in siteConfig.js: `let cached = null` + `loadSiteConfig()` returns cached without refetch, and `useSiteConfig()` only fetches when `cached` is still null. Admin edits bump the server, but any already-mounted pages (or pages subsequently SPA-navigated to without a full reload) keep the stale snapshot. Fix: export `invalidateSiteConfig()` from siteConfig.js (sets `cached = null`) and call it inside SiteConfigAdmin after a successful save/reset so the next useSiteConfig call refetches. The pytest JUnit XML is at /app/test_reports/pytest/iter18_cms.xml (15 passed, 0 failed).
